title: Sequential Pipeline - Three Communication Modes Fair Comparison
description: All three configs run on the same codebase with improved code context retrieval. 50 SWE-bench Lite issues (20 easy, 20 medium, 10 hard).
codebase_version: v2 (with smart code context retrieval, function region extraction, grep fallback)

all_three_succeed.interpretation: Baseline issues solvable regardless of communication architecture

only_MP_succeed.interpretation: Rare cases where message-passing simplicity outperforms structured communication (possible noise from stochastic LLM)

only_BB_succeed.interpretation: Issues where structured blackboard state (without NL noise) was essential

only_Hybrid_succeed.interpretation: Issues where combining structured BB state with NL reasoning context provided unique advantage

BB_and_Hybrid_but_not_MP.interpretation: Issues where structured state access (BB component) was the key differentiator vs pure message passing

MP_and_BB_but_not_Hybrid.interpretation: Issues where Hybrid's extra context may have caused noise or confusion

MP_and_Hybrid_but_not_BB.interpretation: No issues resolved by both MP and Hybrid but not BB

all_three_fail.interpretation: Issues beyond the capability of this pipeline regardless of communication mode (52% of total)

contribution_decomposition.description: Separating the effect of code improvements from communication architecture changes

code_improvement_effect.label: A-Seq v1 -> A-Seq v2 (same comm mode, improved code)
code_improvement_effect.explanation: Code context retrieval (smart truncation, grep fallback) improved resolve rate by +4pp even without changing communication architecture

pure_blackboard_effect.label: A-Seq v2 -> B-Seq (same code, MP -> Blackboard)
pure_blackboard_effect.explanation: Switching from message-passing to blackboard communication added +20pp resolve rate. This is the pure architectural effect of structured shared state.

pure_hybrid_effect.label: A-Seq v2 -> C-Seq (same code, MP -> Hybrid)
pure_hybrid_effect.explanation: Switching from message-passing to hybrid communication added +22pp resolve rate. Hybrid combines BB structured state with NL context from previous agents.

hybrid_vs_blackboard.label: B-Seq -> C-Seq (Blackboard -> Hybrid)
hybrid_vs_blackboard.explanation: Hybrid marginally outperforms pure Blackboard (+2pp), suggesting NL context provides small additional benefit on top of structured state.

attribution_table.interpretation: For both B-Seq and C-Seq, ~83-85% of the total improvement over the Day 2 baseline comes from the communication architecture change, while only ~15-17% comes from code improvements. This validates that communication architecture is the dominant factor.

token_efficiency_analysis.interpretation: Despite higher total token cost, B-Seq and C-Seq are 2x more token-efficient per resolved issue. B-Seq is the most efficient (72,932 tokens/resolve vs 151,574 for A-Seq).

key_findings: 1. Blackboard communication dramatically outperforms message-passing (+20pp pure architectural effect)
2. Hybrid slightly outperforms pure Blackboard (+2pp), but the difference is small
3. Communication architecture accounts for 83-85% of the improvement over baseline; code changes account for 15-17%
4. No config can solve hard issues consistently (0-10% resolve rate for hard difficulty)
5. 52% of issues (26/50) are unsolvable by any communication mode — these represent fundamental capability limits
6. 42% of issues (21/50) show different outcomes depending on communication mode — this is where architecture matters
7. Hybrid uniquely solves 7 issues that neither MP nor BB can solve, suggesting the NL+structured combination provides genuine value
8. BB uniquely solves 4 issues, suggesting pure structured state is sometimes better than noisy hybrid context
9. B-Seq is the most token-efficient per resolved issue (72,932 tokens vs 85,731 for C-Seq and 151,574 for A-Seq)
